recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not change Timing back to BackboneElement; if rendered Structure tables still hide BackboneType for Timing, address that separately under the unresolved FHIR-50466/tooling path.
issue_request: FHIR-17403 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 technical correction asking that the Timing datatype Structure and UML representations agree by showing Timing as BackboneElement rather than Element while still allowing modifierExtension.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN revision 14165, represented in git as ada2e0c9c1c1d9f55da7212a82d639e2dad4832f, which changed the Timing spreadsheet root type from Structure to BackboneElement.
additional_context: The current specification no longer uses the STU3 literal BackboneElement hierarchy for datatype roots that carry modifier extensions. Commit cbdf7d1e55dc4bfa1dc30fc526edee0491e05782 rebuilt the abstract datatype framework, introduced BackboneType, and changed Timing from BackboneElement to BackboneType. Current fhir.ini keeps the datatype pages and diagrams active and marks Timing/BackboneType normative. BackboneType is the DataType-derived base for datatypes that can carry modifierExtension, while BackboneElement is reserved for elements inside resources. Later FHIR-26878 treats Timing as a BackboneType subclass. FHIR-50466 and Zulip discussion show a separate unresolved rendered-page display concern, not a final source-edit decision for this seed.
reconciliation: An empty no-change audit commit was published. Current authoritative source already expresses the corrected hierarchy for the current model: Timing derives from BackboneType, and the active datatype diagrams include BackboneType with Timing under it.

related_jiras.note: Published R5 issue about the BackboneType list explicitly treats Timing as one of the datatypes deriving from BackboneType.
Triaged R6 issue reports rendered Structure tables not labeling BackboneType-derived datatypes as such; unresolved and outside this applied/published source-edit decision.
